cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.

Under the general direction of the Department Undergraduate Programs and Advising Director, the incumbent applies professional concepts to independently provide prescriptive advice on academic policies and procedures for the academic department, including major and minor requirements, and all aspects of course requirements for degree or program completion. They thoughtfully plan student schedules within the constraints of academic course and faculty conflicts, promoting time to degree, and campus guidelines. The incumbent works independently and as part of a collaborative team, receiving assistance on more complex issues.

The work modality for this position is REMOTE, which requires a telecommuting agreement and adherence to the UC Santa Cruz Telecommuting/Remote Work Guidelines. The employee shall be available in a full-time capacity during assigned telecommuting work hours (M & F, 8 a.m.-5 p.m. and TWTH 10:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. Pacific Time). While telecommuting/remote working, the employee is responsible for ensuring a worksite environment suitable for accomplishing their regular job duties during scheduled hours of work, as they would if they were working at the regular UCSC worksite.
Attention to detail and accuracy in highly detailed administrative work across multiple systems.
Training in FERPA and campus enterprise systems such as AIS, CourseDog, InfoView, SmartCat, Navigate/Slug Success, web management systems.
Excellent record keeping and consistent use of systems.
Basic knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.
Knowledge of departmental courses and majors.
Cross-cultural competency and interpersonal skills sufficient to work with diverse populations.
Knowledge of department / school / college policies, procedures, and requirements.
Effective skills in judgment and ability to use discretion on sensitive and confidential matters.
Abilities in problem identification and solving; reasoning and decision making; ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Strong written communication skills.
Strong verbal communication skills, including active listening and note-taking skills.
Ability to follow written and verbal instructions.
Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines.
Strong organizational and planning skills.

Demonstrated research, statistical, and analytical skills with ability to recall, retrieve, and communicate detailed information quickly, accurately, and clearly both verbally and in writing, including preparation of concise written summaries.

Demonstrated computer skills sufficient for preparation and management of a large volume of email, shared documents, databases and spreadsheets using standard office systems (Microsoft, Google Suite (Drive, Apps), Adobe, Zoom), shared servers, and the ability to learn new systems.
Ability to work independently with general supervision and as a collaborative team member.
Knowledge of barriers to student success and intervention techniques to help students overcome difficulties.
